checks.claim: FERC's show-cause proceeding found PJM's tariff unjust for lacking co-location rules and, in December 2025, ordered new transmission services and behind-the-meter generation rules for co-located large loads; compliance filings were still in flight at capture.
checks.evidence: Troutman Energy Report (June 2026) reports that on June 18, 2026 FERC accepted in part and rejected in part requests for rehearing of its December 18, 2025 order in Docket EL25-49-002, and directed further PJM compliance on behind-the-meter generation rules. The shipped sentence is pre-June 2026 and treats the compliance stage as still open at capture without the rehearing order.
checks.correction: FERC's show-cause proceeding found PJM's tariff unjust for lacking co-location rules and, in December 2025, ordered new transmission services and behind-the-meter generation rules for co-located large loads; on June 18, 2026 (EL25-49-002) it ruled on rehearing, set aside parts of that order, and directed further PJM compliance on the behind-the-meter rules.

checks.claim: The $1.8B program (16 TAC §25.513, adopted May 2026) funds critical facilities under 2.5 MW to install a hybrid backup package
checks.evidence: The cited EnergyChoiceMatters article (dated 2026-05-08) describes the program as one that will provide loans and grants to qualifying critical facilities and lists the required mix as natural gas or propane generation, battery storage, and solar generation. The fetched text does not state the $1.8B figure, the 16 TAC §25.513 rule number, the adoption date, or the 2.5 MW threshold. The article's technology list does support the shipped point that nuclear is not an eligible source. Main session: the row's second source (PowerGen Enterprises TBPP guide, fetched) states the $1.8 billion, the 2.5 MW threshold and adoption on May 7, 2026; the Texas Register (January 2026 proposed rules) titles new 16 TAC 25.513 as the TBPP rule. Shipped text stands.
